summary: Harnett County's Cameron Hill held the North Carolina Forest Service's first lookout tower (1926), replaced by a steel tower in 1951. No source describes the site today.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: First North Carolina Forest Service fire lookout tower: wooden, with 60-foot juniper corner poles and an 8 x 8 ft glassed cabin; a 1926-28 state report gives 65 ft
100-foot creosoted wood tower erected August 19, 1938; a 1940 state report credits SCS Camp 18 as a cooperative project, and the Forest Lookouts page says the CCC erected it
A steel tower replaced the earlier wood tower
In March 1965 William Holder and his wife were in the tower when an Air Force truck landed about 200 feet away (Statesville Record and Landmark report, quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1926-28 state report gives the first tower as 65 ft; the September 1926 account gives 60-foot corner poles, which are not a total height. The story reports both.

sources.title: Watch Tower at Cameron Hill to Locate Forest Fires, July 18, 1926

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate: tnlandforms lists two Cameron Hill entries (EZ 3144 at 35.27972, -79.10749, and EZ 3297 'Cameron Hill (old)' at 35.28027, -79.09888) a short distance apart, and us-nc-cameron-hill-old already has a story drawn from the same Forest Lookouts page. One record should be merged or hidden. The sources do not say which entry matches the 1926 site or the 1951 steel tower. No source read says what stands on the hill today or whether the public may visit. Not fetched: a Cameron Hill Tower photograph record at lib.digitalnc.org (record 18541), which may carry a usable image credit.
